newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit stays weak but fall seen limited.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit stays weak but fall seen limited.

text.p: The ringgit remained weak against the dollar in early Asian trading on continued selling by offshore players, dealers said.

"There was a bit of selling out of Sydney this morning but players were not really serious about pushing up the dollar," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank. "Dollar/ringgit looks a bit toppish at the moment."
Dollar gains were likely to be capped at 2.6500, he said.
Trading was limited by a holiday in Japan.
At 0230 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.6380/410 to a dollar. It hit a 38-month low of 2.6450 during London trading on Friday.
Dealers said they expected dollar/ringgit trading to remain volatile due to thin volume and wide spreads.
"The market is still quoting 30 to 50 points spread, so we should continue to see sharp movements," said a European bank dealer in Kuala Lumpur.

He said he expected some position-squaring ahead of the return of Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad from a two-month leave on Tuesday. "Mahathir is likely to comment on the current market situation," he added.
Dealers said there was no sign of Bank Negara's presence in the market this morning.
The central bank had stayed out of the market despite the ringgit sliding by more than five percent against the dollar last week.
